compiled_state.description:
## Summary
Ticket write operations fail hard on git `index.lock` contention and NEVER self-heal:
a single interrupted/crashed commit leaves a stale
`.git/worktrees/<tracker>/index.lock` that wedges **every** subsequent ticket write
(`comment`, `edit`, `create`, `link`, `tag`, …) until a human manually removes it. Even
*transient* contention (two clones committing at once) surfaces as a hard error with no
retry. Locks should be transient and ticket operations should retry + reclaim provably-stale
locks to be self-healing.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Drive any ticket write through `rebar._store.event_append.stage_and_commit` (e.g.
   `rebar comment <id> "..."`).
2. Simulate an interrupted commit by leaving a stale git index lock:
   `touch "$(git -C <tracker> rev-parse --git-dir)/index.lock"` (no git process holds it).
3. Run `rebar comment <id> "anything"` again.

Observed in the wild: after an interrupted `rebar comment`, a ~15-minute-old
`/Users/.../.git/worktrees/-tickets-tracker/index.lock` (0 bytes, no owning process per
`lsof`) blocked five consecutive `rebar comment` retries; the store only recovered after a
manual `rm` of the lock file.

## Expected vs Actual
- **Expected:** a transient `index.lock` contention is retried with bounded backoff and
  succeeds once the peer releases; a *provably stale* `index.lock` (no live owning git
  process / older than a threshold) is detected and reclaimed automatically — mirroring the
  stale-lock reclamation rebar ALREADY does for its own mkdir write-lock
  (`_store/lock.py::_mkdir_lock_is_stale` / `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`). Ticket writes are
  self-healing in the common case; only a genuinely-held lock (live peer) waits/fails.
- **Actual:** `stage_and_commit` (`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:145-175`) shells out to
  `git add`/`git commit` and raises `StoreError("Error: git commit failed while holding
  lock: … Unable to create '<gitdir>/index.lock': File exists. Another git process seems to
  be running …")` on the FIRST failure — no retry, no backoff, no stale detection. The
  rebar `_store/lock.py` write lock is held around this, but that lock only reclaims its OWN
  mkdir lock; the git-owned `index.lock` created transiently by `git add`/`git commit` is
  not covered by any retry or staleness check, so one dead commit wedges all writes.

## Context / root cause
Two lock layers exist and only one self-heals:
- `_store/lock.py` (rebar write lock: fcntl + mkdir) — ALREADY reclaims a provably-stale
  mkdir lock (owner stamp `<host>:<pid>`, dead-pid probe).
- git's `index.lock` (created per `git add`/`git commit` inside `stage_and_commit`) — NOT
  covered. Interrupted/killed commits (CI cancellation, `^C`, OOM, a crashed peer) strand it.

The `edf7`/`6818` history in the surrounding comments shows related git-race hardening
(surfacing stderr, healing UU/unmerged paths), but transient/stale `index.lock` itself is
still fatal-on-first-try.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `stage_and_commit` (and the sibling inline committers `txn.py::claim_core`/
      `transition_core`, `compact.py`) retry a git `index.lock` "File exists / Another git
      process seems to be running" failure with bounded exponential backoff (small, capped
      total wait) before surfacing an error
- [ ] A *provably stale* `index.lock` (no live owning git process AND/OR older than a
      configurable threshold) is detected and reclaimed automatically, reusing/mirroring the
      staleness logic in `_store/lock.py` (`_mkdir_lock_is_stale` / `_reclaim_mkdir_lock`);
      a genuinely-held lock (live peer within the window) is NOT stolen
- [ ] A concurrency test: two processes committing to the same tracker serialize and BOTH
      succeed (no spurious hard failure from transient `index.lock` contention)
- [ ] A stale-lock test: a pre-created `index.lock` with no owning process is reclaimed and
      the ticket write succeeds without manual intervention
- [ ] The retry/reclaim is fail-safe: a lock genuinely held by a live peer still waits within
      budget then surfaces a clear, actionable error (never silently drops the write, never
      corrupts the index)
- [ ] No regression to the existing `edf7` stderr-surfacing and `6818` unmerged-path healing
      behavior
compiled_state.title: Ticket writes fail hard on git index.lock — add retry + stale-lock reclamation (self-healing)
